defects: The top and supports still read as simplified primitive geometry rather than realistic manufactured furniture.
The smoked-glass top has no broad window/room reflection; the compatibility-rendered surface remains nearly uniform dark.
The graphite columns and feet show mottled, noisy highlights from the normal-map workflow instead of coherent powder-coated metal.
Godot continues to report a 0.395-inch gap above the floor datum, so the leveler geometry/orientation change did not correct the measured foot contact.
hard_fail_reasons: A neutral viewer still reads the model as blocky/stylized game geometry rather than realistic human-room furniture.
The close capture lacks credible visible fasteners, leg joints, feet, coherent materials, and manufacturing detail.
The production render does not materially approach the photograph’s broad glass reflections or detailed support/foot construction.
incumbent_comparison: V025 refines v024 with a tighter tabletop chamfer and extra material-specific normal maps, but its close capture remains primitive and the added surface response appears mottled rather than physically coherent. desk-v007 remains the current best-so-far even though it does not pass the repaired absolute visual gate.
likely_causes: The scripted model still uses broad bevelled boxes for the primary furniture forms; part count and texture maps do not supply detailed manufactured geometry.

The candidate-local reflection probe and PBR clearcoat are present and the Compatibility renderer supports reflection probes; the actual capture shows only weak, poorly defined broad reflections under the existing room environment.
The new tangent-space normal map produces patchy highlights on metal rather than the restrained fine grain of powder-coated steel.
Godot still measures the lower bound at Y=0.395, indicating the authored levelers do not reach the floor in the imported mesh.
next_action_hypothesis: Do not promote. Inspect the candidate reflection capture and material parameters in the unchanged Compatibility production path; do not assume that switching renderers fixes the visual failure. The next geometry challenger should replace the simple boxed forms with materially higher-fidelity manufactured profiles, make the reflection probe respond coherently to the room window, and verify in Godot that foot contact is Y=0 before visual inspection.

observations.art_direction_fit: The dark silhouette fits the workstation palette, but the desk still looks like simplified CAD/game geometry and the surface finish is not photo-real.
observations.close_up_quality: asset-detail.png shows a plain, dark top, block-shaped support columns and limited legible hardware; metal mottling adds visual noise rather than crafted finish.
observations.gameplay_readability: The desk is recognizable under the two monitors and remains at its normal computer-desk position; gameplay data are not changed by this visual candidate.
observations.geometric_detail: The candidate contains 15,800 triangles, one imported mesh, five material surfaces and named assembly parts, but the visible support and foot shapes remain broad rectangular primitives.
observations.material_realism: The top remains nearly black with no broad room/window reflections. The powder-coated frame has a mottled normal response that does not resemble the smooth fine grain of coated steel.
observations.proportion: The horizontal top, paired supports and T-feet form a recognizable standing desk. Measured lower bound remains Y=0.395 rather than the zero floor datum.
observations.scale_fidelity: Godot reports 66 x 29.605 x 30 inches and no import issues, but the floor gap is measurable and requires correction.
observations.semantic_recognizability: The three-quarter and room views clearly identify a desk, but its visual character is noticeably simplified compared with realistic manufactured furniture.
observations.silhouette_quality: The thin broad top, two columns, and T-feet form a recognizable desk silhouette; the rectangular legs/feet lack the nuanced edge profiles of the reference.
observations.source_resemblance: The render matches the broad top/leg silhouette and dark color. It misses the photograph’s broad glass reflections, richer metal joins, detailed feet and hardware/cable character.
observations.surface_variation: The additional tangent-space normals create patchy mottling on the metal and do not add coherent, material-specific variation to the glass or frame.
observations.technical_integration: Godot 4.7.2 loaded the asset through the RoomScale production path and captured all six standard views with production_path=true. The capture reports gl_compatibility, 235 close-view draw calls, 107,574 primitives, and 30 FPS; this is a harness capture and not a warmed performance benchmark.

close_inspection.evidence: asset-detail.png exposes primitive rectangular supports, weak visible hardware and joins, a largely dark featureless top, and mottled metal normals.

edge_treatment.evidence: The tightened chamfer and narrow edge highlight in asset-profile.png read as a thin finished top edge, although glass material response still fails.

hardware.evidence: No cleanly seated bolts or adjustment-leveler detail is legible; foot contact is also 0.395 inches above the floor datum in the validated bounds.

joins.evidence: The telescoping transitions are simple boxed bands and the top mounting plates/fasteners do not resolve convincingly in asset-detail.png.

manufacturing_detail.evidence: The visible feet, columns, joints and underside hardware remain simplified rectangular forms.

material_response.evidence: The compatibility-rendered glass has no broad environment reflection, and coated metal appears mottled in asset-detail.png.

surface_variation.evidence: The generated normal-map highlights form patchy noise rather than fine, coherent glass and powder-coat response.

thickness.evidence: The horizontal top presents as a thin slab in asset-profile.png, with a distinct edge band.

neutral_viewer_realism.evidence: asset-three-quarter.png and asset-detail.png identify a desk but show a boxy slab-and-column reconstruction with patchy surface response; it reads as simplified/stylized game geometry, not realistic furniture.

photo_character.evidence: Against photo_holder/Sample (2).jpg, the render preserves the desk envelope and dark color but lacks broad glass/window reflections, detailed feet, and the source’s support/hardware character.
